answer: A hillside vineyard is cut into stone terraces, one per agent. Each keeper sets a numbered opal bead in the channel of its terrace, then the warden releases a bucket of water at the top and the bead rides the flow down through each gate. At the nadir pool at the foot, the warden catches the bead, reads its number against the ledger, and checks the opal flash in sunlight, which no glass copy can match. A thousand fake terraces would need a thousand numbered opal beads and a thousand clear channels, with every bead caught at the pool inside one hour.
